criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal sanitary sewage service access (sewage collection and population attendance rates) across municipal headquarters in the Eastern Watersheds (BHL) of Bahia, Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain wording, the study examines legal, administrative, and governance factors: Section 2 reviews Brazil's National Basic Sanitation Law (Lei 11.445/2007) and Freedom of Information Law (Lei 12.527/2011), and Section 3 empirically assesses municipal governance via (a) whether municipalities have elaborated a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB, Table 2) and (b) municipal transparency and e-SIC administrative responsiveness to public data requests (Quadro 1, Table 3), alongside per-capita public/utility investment (Figure 4). Under the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type scope, however, none of the empirically studied factors is a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden on service applicants, documentation/tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing access). PMSB elaboration is macro-level municipal planning background (not even analytically linked to coverage across municipalities, noted mainly as a condition for post-2019 federal budget transfers), e-SIC hurdles concern citizens/researchers requesting public statistics rather than households accessing sanitation, and the brief mention of STJ sewage-tariff jurisprudence in Section 2 is purely doctrinal background with no empirical tariff analysis.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains empirical descriptive evidence (quali-quantitative design) combining secondary municipal administrative indicators from SNIS (2016-2017) and IBGE MUNIC (2017) with primary Freedom of Information requests (e-SIC and physical protocols) filed with 13 municipal governments.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal-level sewage service access outcomes, specifically the population attendance index for sanitary sewage service in 2017 (Table 1) as well as sewage collection (SNIS IN015, Figure 1) and sewage treatment (SNIS IN056, Figure 2) rates in 2016-2017.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis and population (20 municipal headquarters in BHL, Bahia, 2016-2017), descriptive governance/investment exposures (PMSB status, e-SIC data transparency, per-capita sewage investment), sewage coverage outcomes, and descriptive mixed-methods municipal study design are identifiable from the text, although dimensions are presented descriptively side-by-side rather than testing a rule-type access mechanism.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: O presente estudo busca analisar a situação da universalização, investimento e governança do serviço de esgotamento sanitário das sedes inseridas nas bacias hidrográficas do Leste. Para tanto, possui natureza quali-quantitativa, utilizando-se de dados retirados do Sistema Nacional do Saneamento Básico (SNIS), Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) e de requerimentos enviados para as prefeituras municipais através do Sistema de Informação ao Cidadão em sua forma eletrônica (e-SIC) e física.

Para a análise da universalidade dos serviços de esgotamento sanitário, foram selecionados os indicadores de coleta de esgoto, esgoto tratado referido a água consumida (esgoto tratado) e índice de atendimento populacional do serviço de esgoto sanitário.

Os 13 municípios analisados neste indicador representam 84,54% da população da bacia, com um índice de atendimento de 39,39% em 2017. Isto implica em afirmar que em relação à população de toda a bacia (537.298 habitantes), menos de 50% desses habitantes possuem, ao menos, acesso ao serviço de coleta.

No tocante a governança, com destaque para a existência do Plano Municipal de Saneamento Básico, constata-se na Tabela 2, que apesar da previsão do Plano de Saneamento Básico (PMSB) no art. 9º, I, da Lei 11.445 de 2007, após dez anos de sua promulgação (2017), apenas 15% dos municípios inseridos na Bacia (Itabuna, Santa Luzia e Itajú do Colônia) elaboraram o PMSB.

É importante destacar que para estes municípios que não apresentaram todos os dados utilizados lançados no SNIS, foram enviadas solicitações a partir do sistema E-SIC e SIC, que constituem meios para o cidadão pedir informações públicas aos entes.

raw_response.exposure: Municipal sanitation governance and investment indicators: existence/elaboration status of a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB) under Law 11.445/2007, municipal compliance with Freedom of Information requests (Law 12.527/2011 via e-SIC and physical protocols) for sanitation data, and per-capita sewage investment
raw_response.outcome: Municipal sanitary sewage collection rate (SNIS IN015), treated sewage rate relative to water consumed (SNIS IN056), and municipal population sewage-service attendance rate (% of inhabitants served by sewage collection in 2017)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 20 municipalities with headquarters in the Eastern Watersheds (Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste - BHL), Bahia, Brazil (total headquarters population 635,546 in 2017; population attendance rate reported for 12-13 municipalities covering 537,298 inhabitants)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 rule-type scope clarification of Criterion 2. Although the paper empirically reports municipal sewage service coverage (SNIS population attendance and collection rates) alongside municipal governance and investment indicators across 20 municipalities in Bahia, Brazil — which would satisfy the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 — its empirical governance measures are limited to macro-level municipal planning status (whether a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan, PMSB, has been drafted under Law 11.445/2007) and administrative transparency in responding to the researchers' Freedom of Information (e-SIC) requests for statistical data under Law 12.527/2011, plus aggregate per-capita public investment. It does not empirically examine any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, application burdens, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing access).
raw_response.study_design: Descriptive mixed-methods (quali-quantitative) municipal-level study (2016-2017) using secondary administrative data (SNIS, IBGE MUNIC) and primary Freedom of Information (e-SIC and physical) requests
